title: Cowboy

description.main: Cowboy gathers forty years of Richard Prince's work on the American cowboy, from the Marlboro rephotographs of 1980 to the TIME magazine rescans of the 2010s, compiled by the collector and curator Robert M. Rubin and published by Prince's own imprint Fulton Ryder with DelMonico Books and Prestel.
description.extended:
Cowboy gathers forty years of Richard Prince's work on the American cowboy, compiled and edited by the collector and curator Robert M. Rubin and published in 2020 by Prince's own imprint Fulton Ryder with DelMonico Books and Prestel.

The book is a 480-page sewn softcover designed by COMA, with the title printed around the spine and the trimmed edges rather than on the front. Each chapter opens with a short introduction by Rubin, runs through a group of Prince's works and closes with the ephemera behind them, drawn largely from Prince's own library: Marlboro tear sheets, Leonard McCombe's 1949 LIFE photographs that gave the campaign its model, film stills, pulp paperbacks and writing by Larry McMurtry, Louise Erdrich, Kinky Friedman, Charles Portis and Dorothy M. Johnson.

Prince began rephotographing magazine advertisements in the mid-1970s while working in Time Inc.'s tear-sheet department. The cowboys he cropped from Marlboro ads from 1980 onward became his best-known series and a founding gesture of the Pictures Generation. He returned to the subject in the 2010s with Untitled (original cowboy) and Untitled (cowboy), first shown at LACMA in 2017. The library also holds the Gagosian Cowboys catalogue (2013), Karma's New Cowboys (2017), Untitled (Original Cowboy) (2022) and Tell Me Everything (2026).
description.artist_bio: Richard Prince (b. 1949) emerged with the Pictures Generation in late-1970s New York, rephotographing magazine advertisements and presenting the results as his own pictures. The Cowboys, the Jokes, the Nurses and the Girlfriends are his best-known series. The Guggenheim surveyed his work in 2007 with Spiritual America; Museo Jumex opened the survey Tell Me Everything in September 2026.
description.exhibition_context: Not an exhibition catalogue. Specific Object links it to LACMA's Richard Prince: Untitled (cowboy) (3 Dec 2017 to 25 Mar 2018), which first showed Untitled (cowboy) (2015-16) and Untitled (original cowboy) (2013), but the publisher pages make no such claim.

notes: The library holds two copies of this title; one was previously uncatalogued. Second copy acquired from Allgorithim: https://store.allgorithim.com/products/cowboy-richard-prince Not signed. First edition. Edited and introduced by Robert M. Rubin; designed by COMA; printed and bound by Kösel, Altusried-Krugzell; print run 5,000; winner, Best Dutch Book Designs 2019 and AIGA 50 Books | 50 Covers 2020. Sewn softcover, 480 pp per Prestel and the LC record (484 pp per the Best Dutch Book Designs record and Dashwood Books), 573 colour and 173 b/w illustrations. The Allgorithim listing's 'hardcover, 208 pp, approx 11.5 x 14 in' does not match the published edition or the shop's own photos, which show the standard sewn softcover; the Artsy mirror of the same listing calls it a soft cover book. Prestel and Penguin Random House product pages are gone (out of print); the DelMonico page is used as the publisher URL. Cover image is the publisher's product render (shows spine); a straight-on front-cover crop from the Allgorithim photo is saved in the session scratchpad as an alternative.
